correctness.rationale: For each m>=2 and 0<alpha<1, enumerate the three leaf ball branches and two center branches; every active F Jacobian decomposes as D+R with ||D||2<=1 and ||R||F^2<=m+m^2h^2. Strict concavity produces an open all-global-leaf versus singleton-hub branch; a positive local pair attains sqrt(m((1-h)^2+mh^2)). Squeezing these analytic bounds proves all three fixed-exponent regimes and moving-alpha logarithmic profile. Complex inputs reduce through the 1-Lipschitz coordinate modulus map. Standalone random, branch and critical-window checks ran successfully, and are corroborative rather than infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The result answers the motivated question of how vertexwise noise in a nonlinear fractional graph average propagates to edge gradients. A sharp change in the growth exponent across alpha=1/2, accompanied by an explicitly identified universal 1/log m crossover, is an all-size structural phenomenon not resolved by known one-signal contraction estimates; the positive strict active-cell witness identifies the mechanism. It has quantitative stability content beyond a routine parameter substitution.
